summary: Iter76 — end-to-end verification of Truck Cleaning batch: month scheduler, edit dialogs, review engine, driver scent card, bedding inventory. 29 new backend tests (test_iter76_tc_batch.py) — 28/29 pass; the one failure is a real bug (see rca). Frontend smoke-tested: month calendar renders 42 day cells, prev/next + TODAY + month label all present; clicking a job chip opens the big-font edit dialog with all 5 required data-testids (tc-edit-date/cabs/status/save/delete); Inventory tab renders 9 items with correct 5 bedding + 4 fresheners grouping, LOW badges + stock counters + +/− + +10 restock buttons; AI Offers tab has the Review Engine card (tc-review-engine + tc-review-url-input + tc-review-save); Jobs tab has 29 tc-job-scent-* palette icons; public /tc/scent/{token} page renders the branded card with 8 scents + 10 upgrades + LOCK IT IN submit; invalid token shows tcs-invalid. FULL regression: 116/117 pytest pass across iter72–76 (fixed 3 stale assertions in iter73 + iter75 tests to accept the batch's expanded 19-item UPSELL_META catalog).

minor.issue: Empty payload {} returns 200 (not 400 'Nothing to update' as spec requires). Root cause in truck_cleaning_sched.py line 179: `if payload.window or payload.window == "":` always fires because the Pydantic default for window is `""`. So `upd` is never empty and the 'Nothing to update' guard never trips. Same latent risk on `status` since default is `""` (but that field uses `if payload.status:` which is safe). Fix: use `Optional[str] = None` for window (and any other truly-optional string), or explicitly skip window when it equals its default AND was not user-supplied (Pydantic can distinguish via `model_fields_set`).

ui_bugs.issue: Color legend (crewed/needs-crew/done) is rendered visually (lines 100-104) but has NO data-testid — makes automated testing brittle. Suggest adding data-testid="tc-sched-legend" to the wrapping div.

Today's cell is highlighted with an amber ring (isToday check line 76) but there's no data-testid="tc-cal-today" marker as implied by the spec. Consider adding it to the highlighted cell for testability.

issues: Cooling Gel Pillow showed 'available: -1' after backend adjust tests ran stock below committed count. This is a real edge-case bug: the inventory display computes `available = stock - committed` and does not floor at zero, so scheduled jobs holding upsells while stock is below the committed count produces a negative badge. Cosmetic only, but confusing to operators. Fix: floor `available` at 0 or add a warning color when negative.

critical_code_review_comments: truck_cleaning_sched.py update_job: JobUpdateIn.window default `""` + the `payload.window == ""` check together mean `upd` always contains window="", breaking the 'Nothing to update' guard. This is the root cause of the empty-payload bug. Use Optional[str]=None (or Pydantic model_fields_set) to distinguish 'not provided' from 'explicitly cleared'. Same subtle risk on TechUpdateIn.phone and JobUpdateIn.status.

truck_cleaning.py PRODUCT_IDS excludes bed_change from inventory (correct for spec), but bed_change IS still in scent card upgrades (correct). The two 'product' concepts diverge in one line — worth a comment near PRODUCT_IDS explaining that bed_change is a service, not stock.

truck_cleaning_field.py _remind_job overwrites reschedule_token & scent_card_token on EVERY reminder call if not already present. Fine for first reminder, but if a job's tokens are somehow re-generated later, old public links break. Consider atomicity via $setOnInsert-style logic (find_one_and_update with $set only when field missing).

truck_cleaning_field.py scent_card_submit at line 379 hardcodes `client.get("rate", 150)` — this duplicates the same reprice logic in truck_cleaning_sched.update_job. Consider a shared _reprice(job, cabs, upsells, client) helper to avoid drift.

rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE (empty-payload update accepted): In /app/backend/routes/truck_cleaning_sched.py, JobUpdateIn.window is declared `Field("", max_length=30)` — Pydantic gives it default `""`. In update_job() the guard is `if payload.window or payload.window == "":` — the second branch is True whenever payload.window equals its own default (i.e., always when the caller omits window), so `upd["window"] = ""` is always assigned. Therefore `upd` is never empty on an empty payload, and the intended `raise HTTPException(400, 'Nothing to update')` guard never fires. REPRODUCTION: `curl -X POST /api/truck-cleaning/jobs/{JID}/update -d '{}'` → 200 OK with an update that writes window="". EXPECTED per spec: 400 'Nothing to update'. FIX (recommended): change JobUpdateIn.window to `Optional[str] = None`, then guard becomes `if payload.window is not None: upd["window"] = payload.window`. Apply the same pattern to TechUpdateIn.phone. MITIGATION APPLIED BY TESTING AGENT: none — this is business logic. Test suite documents the bug in test_iter76_tc_batch.py::TestJobEdit::test_update_empty_payload_400 which will flip to green after the fix.
